excerpts.text: **Constitutional Convention**, (1787), in U.S. history, convention that drew up the [Constitution of the United States](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Constitution-of-the-United-States-of-America). Stimulated by severe economic troubles, which produced radical political movements such as [Shays’s Rebellion](https://www.britannica.com/event/Shayss-Rebellion), and urged on by a demand for a stronger central government, the convention met in the Pennsylvania State House in [Philadelphia](https://www.britannica.com/place/Philadelphia) (May 25–September 17, 1787), ostensibly to [amend](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/amend) the Articles of [Confederation](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Articles-of-Confederation). All the states except [Rhode Island](https://www.britannica.com/place/Rhode-Island-state) responded to an invitation issued by the [Annapolis Convention](https://www.britannica.com/event/Annapolis-Convention) of 1786 to send delegates. Of the 74 deputies chosen by the state legislatures, only 55 took part in the proceedings; of these, 39 signed the [Constitution](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Constitution-of-the-United-States-of-America). The delegates included many of the leading figures of the period. Among them were [George Washington](https://www.britannica.com/biography/George-Washington), who was elected to preside, [James Madison](https://www.britannica.com/biography/James-Madison), [Benjamin Franklin](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Benjamin-Franklin), [James Wilson](https://www.britannica.com/biography/James-Wilson-United-States-statesman), [John Rutledge](https://www.britannica.com/biography/John-Rutledge), [Charles Pinckney](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Charles-Pinckney), [Oliver Ellsworth](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Oliver-Ellsworth), and [Gouverneur Morris](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Gouverneur-Morris).

excerpts.text: The **Constitutional Convention** took place in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") from May 25 to September 17, 1787.[[1]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJillson200931,_38-1) While the convention was initially intended to revise the league of states and the first system of [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States") under the [Articles of Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Articles_of_Confederation "Articles of Confederation"),[[2]](#cite_note-2) leading proponents of the Constitutional Convention, including [James Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison "James Madison") of Virginia and [Alexander Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Hamilton "Alexander Hamilton") of New York, sought to create a new frame of government rather than revise the existing one.

It was voted on by the delegates, inscribed on parchment by [Jacob Shallus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Shallus "Jacob Shallus") with engraving for printing, and [signed by 39 of 55 delegates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signing_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Signing of the United States Constitution") on September 17, 1787.
